title: Wheat Production Technology & Nutrient Protocol for NWPZ and NEPZ
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal
region: North Western & North Eastern Plains (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Bihar)
content: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a premier Rabi cereal crop. Optimal sowing window is November 1 to November 15 for timely sown irrigated conditions. Late sowing after November 25 causes terminal heat stress and reduces grain yield by 35-40 kg/ha per day of delay. Recommended varieties: DBW 187 (Karan Vandana), DBW 303 (Karan Vaishnavi), HD 3086, HD 2967, and PBW 725. Seed rate: 100 kg/ha for normal sowing; 125 kg/ha for late-sown conditions. Use Zero Till Seed-cum-Fertilizer Drill or Happy Seeder directly into paddy residue to conserve moisture and curb stubble burning. Spacing: 20-22.5 cm row-to-row spacing at 4-5 cm depth. Nutrient management: Recommended NPK dose is 150:60:40 kg/ha for NWPZ. Apply 1/3rd Nitrogen, full Phosphorus and Potassium as basal dose. Top-dress remaining nitrogen in two equal splits: 1/3rd at first irrigation (CRI stage) and 1/3rd at second irrigation (boot stage). In zinc-deficient soils, apply Zinc Sulphate (heptahydrate 21%) @ 25 kg/ha basally or spray 0.5% ZnSO4 with 0.25% unslaked lime at tillering.
